prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1340; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss by phone. Insured reports a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane roadway. Other vehicle left the scene before exchanging information, though insured obtained a partial plate. Insured reports neck and back pain at the scene and was transported to urgent care. Claim opened under bodily injury and property damage coverages. Police report requested.

Entry 2: Police report received. Officer noted the other vehicle's driver changed lanes into the insured's lane. Witness statement from a passenger in a third vehicle is consistent with the insured's account. Liability appears probable against the unidentified driver. Partial plate run through state database; registered owner identified and contacted by letter.

Entry 3: Claimant's attorney has filed a notice of representation. All further contact to go through counsel. Attorney's office requested the claim file and medical authorizations. Authorizations sent. Attorney indicates claimant has ongoing neck and back strain, with physical therapy recommended by the treating physician. Demand package expected once treatment is complete.

Entry 4: Reviewed property damage estimate for insured vehicle. Repair shop reports rear quarter panel and passenger door damage consistent with a sideswipe impact. Rental car authorized for the repair period under the policy's rental provision. Medical records received from urgent care and primary care physician, documenting cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm. No prior claims for the same body regions found in index search.

Entry 5: Spoke with claimant's attorney regarding status. Physical therapy is ongoing and the treating physician expects improvement over the coming months. Reserves reviewed and adjusted to reflect medical treatment to date. Liability position remains favorable. Will follow up upon receipt of the treatment summary and any demand from counsel. Diary set for review.
